obligations.note: The change adds coapplicant_tax_id to ApplicantFields.ALL, a scope path, and the description says it reuses the existing persistence pipeline. A tax identifier is NPI by the obligation's own wording, but the field is not added to NpiRegistry.FIELDS or to the approved mortgage.npi_fields, so it is persisted unsealed; the exhaustive EncryptionControlTest only enumerates the registry, so its pass does not cover the new field.

Retention.purge now removes coapplicant_tax_id explicitly, which looks correct. However, the only registered control test, RetentionControlTest#sampledPurgeRespectsHold, is labelled sample while the obligation requires exhaustive evidence, and the CI reports' provenance is doubtful (see CHG-4).
Ticket CHG-26624 was approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-21, before review. Its components (mortgage.cases, mortgage.retention, mortgage.control-tests) cover all three touched paths.
Declan Farrell, a change_approver for baseline-mortgage who is not the author, gave a code_review approval on head commit cebee5c.
The change has a single commit, and both approvals name that head commit.

run.json reports success on the head commit from ci-runner-08, started 2026-10-22T17:19Z. The attached JUnit reports were produced on hostname dev-laptop-7.local at 2026-10-23T13:51, with duplicated suite entries, so they cannot be tied to the CI run on the final commit.

ControlFixtures.java is under the protected path apps/baseline-mortgage/src/test/java/controls/*. Rachel Stein (control_owner, controls-office, outside the author's lending-eng team) approved the head commit.

None of the code covered by the ledger entries is altered by this change: Approvals, Policy and Underwriting in baseline-mortgage, and the payments payments, audit and routes code. No existing evidence lapses.

summary: The change introduces a co-applicant tax identifier, which is NPI under ENC-1, without registering it in NpiRegistry or the approved npi_fields list. It is therefore persisted unsealed through the existing pipeline, and the exhaustive encryption control test cannot detect this because it enumerates only registered fields. No exception in the register covers this deviation. Separately, the JUnit reports appear to come from a developer workstation a day after the recorded CI run, and RET-1 has only sample-level control evidence. The process approvals (ticket, code review, control owner) are otherwise in order, but the ENC-1 violation requires rejection.
